message: fix(gsc): clamp month-based date ranges instead of overflowing short months (#133)
statement:
GSC month-based date ranges overflow when the start date lands in a shorter month

`resolveDateRange` in the GSC search analytics feature computes the start of `last_3_months`, `last_6_months`, `last_12_months` and `last_16_months` by subtracting calendar months from the end date. When the end date's day-of-month doesn't exist in the target month, the result rolls forward into the following month instead of landing on the last day of the target month.

Example: `resolveDateRange({ dateRange: "last_3_months" }, new Date("2026-06-03T00:00:00Z"))` yields an end date of `2026-05-31`. The start date should be `2026-02-28`, since 31 February doesn't exist. Instead it overflows into March, so the range is shorter than requested and the start date is wrong.

The 16-month floor that limits how far back a request can go has the same bug. For a "today" of `2026-06-30`, the floor should be `2025-02-28`. It currently overflows past that date.

Expected: any month-based subtraction keeps the same day-of-month when the target month has it. Otherwise it clamps to the target month's last valid day. This applies to all four month-based ranges and to the 16-month floor, with all calculations in UTC. Day-based ranges (`last_7_days`, `last_28_days`) and explicit start/end dates must behave as before.
